_readme: Commercial-intent keyword library, built from evidence rather than from a keyword tool.
TWO SOURCES, BOTH REAL:
1. Google Search Console 'most common referring anchor text', exported 2026-08-31.
These are the words other sites and our own legacy pages actually use to link to
us. They are the closest thing we have to observed demand, and they cost nothing.
2. The category names we publish, which is what a crawler currently matches against.
WHAT THE ANCHOR DATA SAYS. The top four anchors are 'english', 'home' and two bare
URLs — navigational, carrying no topic. Descriptive anchors begin at rank 5 and are
almost all SINGULAR head terms: lock cylinder, lever handle, lock case, panic exit
device, door closer, sliding hook lock, grip handle set, stainless steel handle.
Our category names are plural. 'deadbolts' is the one anchor that arrives plural,
and it is also the one that matches our page name exactly.
HOW MUCH THAT MATTERS — SAY IT HONESTLY. Google stems singular and plural together;
'lever handle' and 'Lever Handles' are not two different queries to it. Do NOT rewrite
page titles chasing the singular form. What the anchor list is genuinely good for is
confirming WHICH of our fifteen categories carry external link equity at all, and
which five have never been linked with a descriptive word by anybody.
INTENT TIERS. `informational` answers a question, `commercial` compares or qualifies a
supplier, `transactional` asks to buy. A B2B hardware buyer moves through all three,
and our pages currently speak almost entirely in product nouns with no supplier or
buying vocabulary in the body copy. That is the measurable gap, not the plural.
Run scripts/audit-keyword-coverage.mjs against the built export for real numbers.
Do not add a term here because it looks good in a report — add it when a real buyer
or a real referring link used it.
